coverage_contract.rule: Every manuscript built by paper/Makefile and every root manuscript PDF licensed by REUSE.toml must appear exactly once in artifacts. A rejected artifact must not be built, licensed, or present as a shipped manuscript.

artifacts.title: Tail Certificates and Achievement-Set Geometry for Erdős Problems 249 and 257
artifacts.claim_scope: Gateway exposition for Erdős Problems 249 and 257. For #249 it records the exact dyadic-section rank 2^e+1 for e >= 1, infinite-dimensionality, the explicit finite Farey denominator exclusion, and diagonal certificates through t = 82, but no instance at t = 83 or unbounded family. For #257 it records checked restricted-support geometry and the remaining half-value and 1/21 branches. Both problems remain open, and the shared Lambert-series change of variables transfers no irrationality theorem.

artifacts.title: How a Lean Repository Turns Formal Proofs into a Checked Public Release
artifacts.claim_scope: A first-principles architecture and access guide to the public Lean source, reviewed claim record, authored documents, generated views, release flow, CI jobs, and human trust boundary. A later historical example illustrates the limit of explicitly recorded checks; the guide adds no mathematical result.

artifacts.title: From a Cold Clone to a Proof Receipt
artifacts.claim_scope: A case study of zero-build corpus navigation, explicit authority boundaries, replayable agent-session receipts, focused changed-cone builds, and exact cached dependency-index validation in this repository. It does not claim autonomous proving, optimal reasoning, external mathematical novelty, or demonstrated transfer to another project.

artifacts.title: The Binary Totient Series: a claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős Problem 249
artifacts.claim_scope: Claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős Problem 249. It distinguishes checked premises and finite certificates from open obligations: the level-e dyadic-section rank is 2^e+1 only for e >= 1; the full span is infinite-dimensional; the finite Farey computation excludes denominators up to the stated bound; and diagonal certificates exist through t = 82, with neither t = 83 nor an unbounded family supplied. Irrationality remains open.

artifacts.title: Reciprocal Mersenne Subseries: a claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős Problem 257
artifacts.claim_scope: Claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős Problem 257. It separates checked finite-support and restricted-achievement-set structure from the missing Booleanisation and tail steps. No finite rank-at-least-two support represents 1/21; the primitive 2p+3q cone has the stated coverage and recurrent multiplicities, but the eventual affine-supercapacity regime survives. The universal, half-value, and 1/21 membership questions remain open.

artifacts.title: Exact Ranks for the Dyadic Sections of Euler’s Totient
artifacts.claim_scope: Standalone exposition of Erdős Problem 249, ordered unconditional results first: the exact level-e dyadic totient section rank 2^e+1 for e >= 1 and the resulting infinite-dimensionality; the explicit finite-Farey denominator exclusion; the phi*mu Lambert weight separating #249 from the settled omega/Omega/tau series; and scoped method no-go theorems. Lean checks diagonal certificates for every t <= 82, but supplies neither t = 83 nor the unbounded family equivalent to irrationality. The problem remains open.

artifacts.title: Forced Structure in Mersenne Subseries
artifacts.claim_scope: Standalone exposition of Erdős Problem 257 led by exact finite-period noncollapse, necessary structure for any rational-valued infinite support, and achievement-set geometry. Duverney–Tachiya settle squarefree support for every power-of-two base, including base 2; this does not cover arbitrary bases b >= 3. The manuscript separately proves that two divisibility-first certificate engines miss this settled value and that irrationality is invariant under finite support changes via checked prefix/tail lemmas. No finite rank-at-least-two support sums to 1/21, while the quotient-greedy classification leaves an eventual affine-supercapacity regime unexcluded. Tao–Teräväinen prove prime support at base 2. Universal Erdős #257, the half-value test, and 1/21 membership remain open.

artifacts.title: Excluding the Bounded Negative Part
artifacts.claim_scope: Exposition of the ErdosProblems.Erdos243 modules. Lean checks constant- and scoped periodic-negative exclusions, eventual vanishing from an eventually bounded negative part plus normalised vanishing, and exclusion of finite normalised negative mass. Eventual strict centring is not an independent hypothesis because normalised vanishing supplies it after a finite shift. Koizumi supplies normalised vanishing for the canonical orbit; boundedness of its negative part is not supplied. Mixed-sign classification and the unbounded divergent-mass branch remain open, so Erdős Problem 243 remains open.

artifacts.title: The Prime-Gap Equivalence and the Integral-Shift Frontier
artifacts.claim_scope: Exposition of the ErdosProblems.Erdos251 module. Lean checks the infinite prime/gap equivalence conditional on summability, denominator collapse for rational dyadic recurrences, unboundedness and non-eventual-periodicity of the actual prime gaps, and the exact local implication from cofinally recurring adjacent small-mismatch tail shifts to failure of eventual integrality. The prime-number-theorem summability and concrete prime-gap-tail instantiation are paper proofs; no theorem supplies the required cofinal adjacent small-mismatch pairs, and Erdős Problem 251 remains open.

artifacts.title: The Three-Prime Running Least Common Multiple
artifacts.claim_scope: The paper proves, using Bugeaud–Laurent's external Hecke–Mahler theorem, that for every pair of distinct primes both the de-duplicated and repeated-running-LCM sums are transcendental; these analytic deductions are not Lean-formalised. For three primes, Lean checks exact logarithmic-cell and finite height-fibre structure, the dyadic block alphabet {2,6,10,30}, residue arithmetic, and the conditional absorption-and-cancellation core. The scan over 106,666 denominator/start pairs is bounded evidence only. Rationality-to-carry identification, the required divisibility, and a cofinal escape producer are unproved; Problem 269 remains open from three primes onward.

artifacts.title: Rational Bases and the Integer-Base Argument
artifacts.claim_scope: Exposition of scoped no-go and counting results for Erdős Problem 1049, not an irrationality theorem. Lean checks scalar-content neutrality, the endpoint exclusion of 2 and 3 under unit hypotheses, four-jet cancellation at the stated rank threshold, a coordinatewise-clearing corridor obstruction and tail recurrence at 3/2, and the elementary height inequality needed by Bundschuh–Väänänen's external criterion at 7/2. The external analytic argument is not formalised. Polynomial-factor, cross-row, primitive-family, nonzero-pair, and analytic-remainder routes remain untreated; the rational-base problem remains open.
